examples.en: I usually have lunch with my friends on weekends.
We took this trip with the whole family for the first time in a while.
If you have time, would you like to have dinner together?

examples.ko: 오래 같이한 친구라서 말하지 않아도 알아요.
examples.en: We've spent so long together as friends that I understand without being told.

examples.ko: 저는 평생을 같이할 친구를 드디어 만났어요.
examples.en: I finally met a friend I want to spend my whole life with.
I'm glad we get to do this project together.

explain: 식사, 시간, 여행, 인생처럼 무언가를 함께 누릴 때 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '같이 먹어요'처럼 풀어 쓰는 게 더 자연스럽고, '같이하다'는 '식사를 같이하다'처럼 조금 격식 있게 들려요. '함께하다'도 비슷한데 더 격식 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Friends who share my goals gathered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 목표가 같아서 한편이 된다는 뜻이에요. 연설이나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people hold the same goal or view and stand together. Common in speeches and writing.

explain_en: It fits things you share or enjoy together: meals, time, trips, a life. In casual speech people just say '같이 먹어요' (eat together); '같이하다' sounds a little more polite, as in '식사를 같이하다'. '함께하다' is similar but more formal.

dis.h: do or spend something together with someone

p.n: 공유하다 needs something to share (info, files); it can't mean doing an activity together.

examples.en: In summer the rain goes on for over a week.
The meeting went on for three hours.

examples.ko: 이 더위는 다음 주에도 계속될 거예요.
examples.en: This heat will continue next week too.
I'm so tired from the nonstop overtime.
My cough kept going for days, so I went to the hospital.
The two people's conversation continued until night.

explain: '계속하다'는 사람이 이어 가는 것이고, '계속되다'는 일이 저절로 이어지는 것이에요. 비·더위·기침·야근처럼 내가 멈추기 어려운 일에 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '계속 공부해요'처럼 '계속'만 부사로 붙여 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 많아요.

phrases.en: The hot weather is continuing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 이어지는 중이라는 뜻이에요. 날씨 이야기에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is still going on now; common when talking about weather.

phrases.en: If your cough continues, go to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 계속 이어질 때의 조건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -(으)면 to give a condition: if it keeps going.

phrases.en: I'm having a hard time because of the continuing heat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 이어지는 일을 꾸며 말해요. 더위·비·추위 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -는 to describe something that keeps going; common with heat, rain, or cold.

explain_en: '계속하다' is when a person keeps something going; '계속되다' is when something just keeps going by itself. It fits things you can't easily stop: rain, heat, a cough, overtime. In everyday speech, '계속' alone as an adverb ('계속 공부해요') is far more common.

dis.h: go on without stopping; has no object

p.n: 이어지다 stresses linking to what came before.

examples.en: This company advertises its new product on TV.
We're advertising our small bakery online.
That actor advertised the new cosmetics.
I made flyers to advertise the new restaurant.

examples.ko: 가게를 광고하지 않으면 손님이 안 와요.
examples.en: If you don't advertise the shop, customers won't come.

examples.ko: 지하철 안에서 광고할 수 있는 자리가 많지 않아요.
examples.en: There aren't many spots to advertise inside the subway.

explain: '광고하다'는 돈을 들여 알리는 느낌이 강하고, '홍보하다'는 돈을 쓰든 안 쓰든 널리 알리는 일을 두루 가리켜요. 친구에게 가게를 알려 주는 건 '소개하다'가 자연스러워요. 'TV 광고', '광고를 보다'처럼 명사 쓰임이 아주 많아요.

phrases.en: We promote the school with a video.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 쓰든 안 쓰든 널리 알리는 일을 두루 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers any effort to spread the word, paid or not.

phrases.en: The new shop is advertising its new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광고하다'와 뜻이 같고, '광고'를 따로 떼어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 광고하다, with 광고 split out as a noun.

phrases.en: I saw an ad for a new movie on the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 보는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who sees the ad.

explain_en: '광고하다' leans toward paid promotion, while '홍보하다' covers spreading the word, paid or not. Telling a friend about a shop is more naturally '소개하다'. The noun is very common: 'TV 광고' (TV ad), '광고를 보다' (watch an ad).

examples.en: In elementary school, I wrote a picture diary every day.
I drew what happened today in my picture diary.

examples.ko: 그림일기는 글솜씨가 없어도 쓸 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: A picture diary is nice because you can write one even without good writing skills.
An old picture diary turned up in the drawer.
Writing a picture diary is one of the vacation homework assignments.
I looked back on the day with my child through a picture diary.

explain: 초등학교 저학년 때 방학 숙제나 수업으로 많이 쓰는 일기예요. 어른이 되어 '그림일기를 쓰다'라고 하면 그림으로 하루를 기록한다는 느낌이에요. '일기를 쓰다'와 같이 동사는 '쓰다'를 써요.

phrases.en: When I was little, I wrote a picture diary every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기는 '쓰다'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Diaries go with the verb 쓰다.

phrases.en: We had picture diary homework during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 숙제로 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often comes up as school homework.

phrases.en: I drew a picture of a puppy in my picture diary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기장 안에 그림을 넣는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting a drawing inside the diary.

explain_en: This is the kind of diary many children write in lower elementary grades as vacation homework or class work. When an adult says '그림일기를 쓰다', it feels like recording the day with drawings. As with '일기를 쓰다', the verb is '쓰다'.

examples.ko: 새 단어는 단어장에 적어 두고 외워요.
examples.en: I write new words in my vocabulary notebook and memorize them.
I carry my vocabulary notebook in my bag.

examples.ko: 단어장이 거의 다 차서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: My vocabulary notebook was almost full, so I bought a new one.
This vocabulary list is organized by topic.
My friend's vocabulary notebook is organized really neatly.
I also have a word list I made on a phone app.

explain: 직접 단어를 적는 공책도, 단어를 모아 놓은 책이나 앱 목록도 단어장이라고 해요. '단어장을 만들다', '단어장에 적다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I made a vocabulary notebook before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부할 단어를 직접 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you collect words to study yourself.

phrases.en: I write unfamiliar words in my vocabulary notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단어를 기록해 둘 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for recording words.
phrases.en_equiv: to write in a vocabulary notebook

phrases.en: I memorize words every day with a vocabulary app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰으로 단어를 공부하는 앱을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An app for studying words on a phone.

explain_en: A handwritten notebook of words, or a printed or app-based word list, can all be called 단어장. It goes with '단어장을 만들다' (make one) and '단어장에 적다' (write in one).

examples.en: The child came down the slide happily.
I tried to climb up the slide but kept slipping.
The playground has swings and a slide.
My younger sibling came down the slide upside down.

examples.ko: 미끄럼틀은 한 명씩 차례대로 타야 해요.
examples.en: You have to take turns going down the slide one at a time.
My child runs over whenever she sees a slide.

explain: '미끄럼틀을 타다'가 짝이 되는 표현이에요. '미끄럽다', '미끄러지다'와 소리와 뜻이 가까워서 같이 기억하면 쉬워요. 놀이터에서 그네, 시소와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The children ride the slide at the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미끄럼틀과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 미끄럼틀.

phrases.en: My younger brother came down the slide and laughed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미끄럼틀을 타고 아래로 내려오는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe sliding down from the top.

phrases.en: The playground slide is very tall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 앞에 붙여 어떤 미끄럼틀인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the place in front tells which slide you mean.

explain_en: The natural collocation is '미끄럼틀을 타다'. Its sound and meaning are close to '미끄럽다' and '미끄러지다', so learning them together helps. It often appears with swings and seesaws at playgrounds.

examples.en: That village is in the northwest of Seoul.
In winter a cold wind blows in from the northwest.
The small lake is in the northwest of the park.
If you walk ten minutes to the northwest, you will find it.
Dark clouds are rushing in quickly from the northwest.
The compass needle is pointing to the northwest.

explain: 한국의 겨울 찬 바람은 북서쪽에서 오는 일이 많아서 날씨 이야기에 자주 나와요. 'ㄱ' 받침 뒤라서 '서'가 [써]로 세게 소리 나고, [북써쪽]이라고 읽어요. 바람 이름은 '북서풍'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: In winter the northwest wind blows hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 북서쪽에서 불어오는 바람을 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for the wind from the northwest.

phrases.en: My school is in the northwest of the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '에 있다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 'e itda' to say where something is.

phrases.en: Go northwest for about an hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'는 가는 방향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Euro' marks the direction you are going.

explain_en: Cold winter winds in Korea often come from the northwest, so this word shows up in weather talk. After the final 'ㄱ' the 'ㅅ' of '서' is tensed, so it is read [buk-sseo-jjok]. The wind itself is called '북서풍'.

examples.en: My stepdad plays with me every weekend.
I cooked together with my stepdad.
Mom and my stepdad got married last year.
Thanks to my stepdad, I got a new family.
I got allowance money from my stepdad.
My stepdad made a delicious dinner for me.

explain: '새아버지'보다 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 짝이 되는 말은 '새엄마'예요. 서류에서는 '계부'라고 하고, 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아빠'나 '아버지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My mom got married this year, so I got a stepfather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새아빠'와 함께 가족이 새로 생겼을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'saeappa' when a new family member joins the family.

phrases.en: My friend has both a stepfather and a stepmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말 '새엄마'와 함께 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with its counterpart 'saeeomma' (stepmother).

phrases.en: My stepfather takes good care of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새아빠'보다 조금 더 공손하고 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more polite and formal word than 'saeappa'.

explain_en: It is a more casual spoken word than '새아버지'. Its counterpart is '새엄마'. On documents the term is '계부', and when addressing him directly people usually say '아빠' or '아버지'.

examples.en: There are ten pairs of shoes in the shoe cabinet.
The shoe cabinet next to the entrance is too narrow.
I tidied the shoe cabinet before the guests came.

examples.ko: 새 운동화를 신발장 맨 위 칸에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I put the new sneakers on the top shelf of the shoe cabinet.

examples.ko: 신발장 문이 안 닫혀서 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: The shoe cabinet door won't close, so I need to fix it.

examples.ko: 우리 집 신발장은 우산도 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Our shoe cabinet can hold umbrellas too.

explain: 한국 집은 현관에서 신발을 벗기 때문에 대부분 현관 쪽에 신발장이 있어요. 신발을 '넣다, 꺼내다, 정리하다'와 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '신발장'이라고 하면 충분히 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Please put your shoes in the shoe rack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발을 보관할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic expression for storing shoes.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in the shoe rack

phrases.en: I took my sneakers out of the shoe rack.
phrases.nuance_ko: '넣다'의 반대 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the opposite action of 'neota' (to put in).
phrases.en_equiv: to take out of the shoe rack

phrases.en: I tidied up the shoe rack on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발장을 깨끗하게 치우고 정돈할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning and organizing the shoe rack.

explain_en: Korean homes have you take off shoes at the entrance, so the shoe cabinet is usually right there. It goes with verbs like '넣다' (put in), '꺼내다' (take out) and '정리하다' (tidy up). In daily speech, '신발장' is perfectly natural.

examples.en: The weather has suddenly gotten quite chilly lately.
I haven't been sleeping well lately.
Has something good been happening to you lately?

examples.ko: 요사이 회사 일이 많아서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: I have so much work these days that I'm swamped.
I haven't heard anything from my friends lately.
I started exercising lately and my body feels lighter.

explain: '요즘', '요새'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '요새'는 '요사이'를 줄인 말이에요. 문장 맨 앞에서 '요사이 어때요?'처럼 안부를 물을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: What have you been up to these days?
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word for this meaning.

phrases.en: I've been tired lately because I have a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요사이'를 줄인 말로 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 'yosai', common in conversation.

phrases.en: Long time no see. How are you these days?
phrases.nuance_ko: 안부를 물을 때 문장 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the start of a sentence to ask how someone is.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '요즘' and '요새'; '요새' is the contracted form of '요사이'. You can put it at the start of a sentence to ask how someone is, as in '요사이 어때요?'.

examples.en: I looked for the information I needed on the web.

examples.ko: 이 웹 사이트는 한국어로도 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can view this website in Korean too.

examples.ko: 웹 디자인을 배우고 싶어서 학원에 등록했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to learn web design, so I signed up at an academy.

examples.ko: 제 친구는 웹 개발자로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend works as a web developer.

examples.ko: 집에서 웹으로 예약하면 훨씬 더 싸요.
examples.en: It's much cheaper if you book on the web from home.

examples.ko: 동생은 웹 소설을 읽느라 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling stayed up all night reading web novels.

explain: '웹'은 보통 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 '웹 사이트', '웹툰', '웹 소설'처럼 써요. 그냥 '인터넷'이라고 해도 되지만, 인터넷 페이지를 말할 때는 '웹'이 자주 나와요. 한국에서는 '웹툰'을 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I check the timetable on the school website.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웹' 뒤에 붙어 인터넷 페이지를 말해요. 줄여서 '사이트'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 웹 attached to 사이트 refers to an internet page; people also just say 사이트.

phrases.en: I read webtoons on the subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷으로 보는 한국식 만화예요. 한국에서 아주 인기가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Korean-style comics read online; very popular in Korea.

phrases.en: I study Korean while reading web novels.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷에서 연재하는 소설이에요. 종이책과 달리 휴대폰으로 읽어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A novel published online in installments, read on a phone rather than on paper.

explain_en: 웹 usually attaches to another word, as in 웹 사이트, 웹툰, and 웹 소설. You could just say 인터넷, but 웹 comes up often when talking about internet pages. Webtoons (웹툰) are very popular in Korea.

examples.en: Every morning the garbage truck passes through our neighborhood.
The garbage truck's noise startled me awake.
They loaded the collected trash onto the garbage truck.
The garbage truck usually comes early in the morning.

examples.ko: 아이들이 청소차를 보면 신나서 손을 흔들어요.
examples.en: When children see the garbage truck, they wave excitedly.
The road is narrow, so even the garbage truck can't get in.

explain: '쓰레기차'라고도 말해요. 쓰레기를 모아 가는 차라서 '쓰레기를 싣다', '쓰레기를 수거하다'와 같이 나와요. 소방차, 구급차처럼 '-차' 이름의 특수한 차 중 하나예요.

phrases.en: A garbage truck is parked in the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy synonym with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Put out the trash before the garbage truck comes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 가져가는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about trash pickup time.

phrases.en: I said hello to the garbage truck driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소차를 운전하는 분을 높여 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to refer to the truck's driver.

explain_en: People also say '쓰레기차'. Since it collects trash, it appears with '쓰레기를 싣다' (load) and '쓰레기를 수거하다' (collect). It's one of the special vehicles with '-차' names, like '소방차' and '구급차'.

en: own older brother (of a male speaker)

examples.en: I have one older brother.
My older brother is three years older than me.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 친형과 같은 방을 썼어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I shared a room with my older brother.
My older brother got married and lives separately.

examples.ko: 친형 때문에 저도 축구를 좋아하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of my older brother, I came to like soccer too.
I borrowed my older brother's phone and made a call.

explain: 남자가 자기 형을 말할 때 '형'이라고 해요. 사촌 형이나 친한 동네 형이 아니라 진짜 형제라고 분명히 하고 싶을 때 '친형'이라고 해요. 여자의 오빠는 '친오빠', 언니는 '친언니'예요.

phrases.en: I have one older brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 보통 '형'이라고만 해요. '친형'은 진짜 형제라고 분명히 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life people just say 'hyeong'. 'Chinhyeong' stresses a real brother.

phrases.en: My older brother works at a company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 높여 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'nim' makes it more respectful when speaking to others.

phrases.en: We are not cousins; we are real brothers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사촌이 아니라 같은 부모의 형제라고 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that you are brothers with the same parents, not cousins.

explain_en: A man calls his older brother 형. Say 친형 when you want to make clear it is your real brother, not a cousin or a friendly older guy from the neighborhood. A woman says 친오빠 or 친언니.

examples.en: I wrote the appointment in my phone calendar.

examples.ko: 캘린더 앱에 친구 생일을 모두 저장했어요.
examples.en: I saved all my friends' birthdays in the calendar app.
Looking at the calendar, next week is a holiday.

examples.ko: 이 캘린더는 한국 공휴일이 다 나와 있어요.
examples.en: This calendar shows all the Korean public holidays.
Tomorrow's meeting time changed in the calendar.
I made a shared calendar with my friend.

explain: 한국에서는 종이 달력은 '달력'을 더 많이 쓰고, 휴대폰 앱이나 컴퓨터 일정표에는 '캘린더'를 많이 써요. 같은 사물이지만 말하는 장면이 조금 달라요. '캘린더에 넣다', '캘린더 공유'처럼 앱 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I put the appointment in my calendar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일정을 앱에 저장할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for saving an event in a calendar app.

phrases.en: I manage my schedule with a calendar app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰의 일정 앱을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the schedule app on a phone.

phrases.example: 친구와 캘린더 공유를 해서 약속 잡기가 쉬워요.
phrases.en: Sharing calendars with my friend makes planning easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일정을 다른 사람과 같이 볼 수 있게 하는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Letting others see your schedule too.

explain_en: For a paper calendar Koreans prefer 달력, while 캘린더 is more common for phone apps and computer schedules. 캘린더에 넣다 and 캘린더 공유 often come up when talking about apps.

examples.en: At the zoo, a panda is eating bamboo.
I bought one panda doll.
A baby panda was born and it was on the news.
Pandas eat and sleep all day.

examples.ko: 친구는 판다를 보러 중국에 가고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My friend wants to go to China to see pandas.

examples.ko: 눈 주위가 까만 판다는 정말 귀여워요.
examples.en: A panda with dark patches around its eyes is really cute.

explain: 한국에서도 판다는 아주 인기 있는 동물이라 '푸바오'처럼 이름이 붙은 판다 이야기가 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 판다는 곰과 비슷해서 '판다 곰'이라고도 하지만 보통 그냥 판다라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The baby panda is really cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린 판다를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a young panda.

phrases.example: 판다 곰은 하루 종일 대나무를 먹어요.
phrases.en: Pandas eat bamboo all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곰과 비슷해서 붙인 말이지만 보통은 '판다'라고만 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mentions the bear resemblance, but people usually just say 판다.

phrases.en: I gave my younger sibling a panda doll.
phrases.nuance_ko: 판다 모양의 인형을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stuffed toy shaped like a panda.

explain_en: Pandas are hugely popular in Korea, and named pandas like 푸바오 often make the news. They're bear-like, so 판다 곰 also exists, but people usually just say 판다.

examples.en: I was startled when a phone call suddenly came in the middle of the night.
The baby woke up and cried in the middle of the night.
The dead of night is quiet, so I end up thinking a lot.
Seoul's night view in the dead of night is really beautiful.
When it became the dead of night, the street grew quiet.
Yesterday I studied for the exam until the dead of night.

explain: 밤이 가장 깊은 때를 말하고, '한밤중'이라고도 해요. 늦은 저녁이나 새벽보다 더 깊은 밤 느낌이라 '한밤에 전화하다'처럼 놀랍거나 예의에 어긋나는 일과 같이 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: It rained a lot in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한밤'과 거의 같고, 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 한밤, and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I had a scary dream and woke up in the middle of the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 밤에 잠에서 깰 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when waking up in the deep of night.
phrases.en_equiv: to wake up in the middle of the night

phrases.en: The street in the middle of the night is very quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 밤의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a scene in the deep of night.

explain_en: It refers to the deepest part of the night and is also said as '한밤중'. It feels deeper than late evening or dawn, so it often appears with surprising or impolite things, like calling someone in the middle of the night.

examples.en: Phew, the exam is finally over.
Phew, luckily I didn't miss the train.
Phew, today was a really hard day.

examples.ko: 휴, 이번 달 월급이 벌써 다 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: Sigh, this month's pay is already gone.

examples.ko: 휴, 이제 겨우 숙제를 다 했어요.
examples.en: Phew, I've only just finished my homework.
Phew, let me catch my breath and start again.

explain: 한숨을 쉬듯 내는 소리로, 안심했을 때와 힘들거나 걱정될 때 둘 다 써요. 소리가 같아서 상황과 표정으로 구분해요. 문자나 메신저에서는 '휴…'처럼 점을 붙여 쓰고, 쉬는 날을 뜻하는 '휴가'의 '휴'와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Phew, today was really hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴'와 비슷하지만 힘들거나 지칠 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '휴', but used more often when tired or worn out.

phrases.en: Phew, I just barely arrived on time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴'보다 숨을 길게 내쉬는 느낌이고 안심했을 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A longer exhale than '휴', often used when relieved.

phrases.en: Phew, I finished all my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴'를 길게 늘인 말로 한숨을 더 크게 쉬는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drawn-out '휴' that sounds like a bigger sigh.

explain_en: A sound like letting out a breath, used both for relief and for fatigue or worry. Since the sound is the same, context and facial expression tell them apart. In texts it is often written with dots, as in '휴…', and it is unrelated to the '휴' in '휴가' (vacation).
